messages:
dmitri: :rotating_light: ALERT: Autoscaler failing to add nodes to gpu-pool-prod, queue growth observed. Root cause unknown yet. paging now.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1955554321 - GPU capacity degradation (autoscale gap) — page routed to oncall.
oncall-bot: @dmitri you are on-call for infra. Please acknowledge.
dmitri: ack, on it. I'm looking at the autoscaler logs and cloud API errors.
sara: seeing lots of CUDA/Xid errors on g2-prod-xx (OOM + Xid 31). Drivers are sporadically killing processes. Logs: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv` shows 99% mem on several nodes.
chris: autoscaler metrics show FailedProvisioning > 200 in last 5m. API errors: QUOTA_EXCEEDED and TIMEOUT. Cloud says we hit region GPU quota, scale requests are being rejected.
dmitri: so two compounding issues: driver instability reducing available GPUs + cloud quota preventing new nodes = queue growth. Good summary.
alex: app queue backlog: 18k tokens waiting, p50 latency spiking from 120ms -> 3.5s, p95 12s. Affected customers: sandbox and some paid Dedicated tenants.
mike: any immediate mitigations we can run to relieve load? Can we evict noncritical jobs or move to a lower-tier model?
dmitri: yes. Step 1: triage & protect critical tenants. Step 2: reclaim capacity by draining unstable nodes. Step 3: temporary routing to fallback smaller models in region-us-east fallback pool.
emily: I'm starting a canary config: route non-enterprise traffic to model-small-v2 and enable caching for repeated prefixes. Pushing now.
sara: moving to cordon + drain nodes showing repeated Xid errors: g2-prod-07, g2-prod-12. Running: `kubectl cordon g2-prod-07 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data g2-prod-07`.
chris: note: some nodes are crashlooping driver pods. Restarting driver via systemd might help: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` (run via ssh job). Doing g2-prod-07 restart now.
alex: alert: autoscaler is still queued but requests are rate-limited by cloud. Ops contact for quota increase is pended (cloud support ticket #CASE-8892). ETA unknown.
dmitri: while we wait, prioritize internal reclaimed capacity. Who can OOM-restart on problem nodes? @sara?
sara: restarting driver on g2-prod-07 succeeded. Node rejoined but a few workloads OOM'd — reclaiming ~1 GPU effective.
mike: routed 30% of requests for sandbox to fallback pool, reduced queue by ~6k. Latency improved to p50 210ms for those requests.
emily: cache hit rate from prefix cache now 18% for repeated prompts, saves ~40 tokens/request. That helps.
dmitri: good. Still need to free more. Chris, can you identify large-batch jobs we can pause (internal CI or heavy evals)?
chris: yes — pausing nightly-eval and internal-bench jobs across the fleet. Command pushed: `cictl pause-job nightly-eval --scope=gpu-prod`
alex: customer impact: two Dedicated tenants saw degraded response times and elevated error rates (5xx). Noting support tickets opened: #SUP-412, #SUP-413. We're informing them.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-1955554321 - page acknowledged by dmitri. Escalation: SRE lead oncall.
dmitri: FYI ops log: driver instability suggests memory leak in driver v525.42 rollout last night. Need root cause analysis later. For now, rollback candidate driver to 520.x? Thoughts?
sara: rollback considered risky but plausible. Alternative: rebooting nodes after drain seems to temporarily stabilize. I'll collect stack traces: `dmesg | grep -i Xid` and GPU logs.
emily: I can quick-toggle quantization for heavy models to reduce memory pressure as a targeted mitigation for 10% of traffic — doing rollout.
mike: after these steps queue dropped from 18k -> 4.2k over 20 minutes. Error rate down 60%. Autoscaler still blocked by quota; cloud case updated.
dmitri: continuing: 1) keep draining unstable nodes 2) pause noncritical jobs 3) route to smaller models and enable prefix caching 4) escalate cloud quota and request urgent increase 5) collect driver logs and open rollback RFC if leak confirmed.
chris: opened follow-up ticket INFRA-966 to track driver rollback plan + test matrix.
alex: sending customer communications: short status note posted to status.redwood.ai and support updated.
dmitri: leaving for handoff in 15m to next oncall (alex). Anyone else join handoff?
emily: I'll stay for follow-up and help with model routing checks.
sara: I'll finish log collection and post gist with traces.
mike: handing over runbook edits to alex: updating autoscaler runbook with cloud quota check + fallback routing playbook.
alex: ack takeover. I'll monitor cloud support and let customers know ETA. Current state: degraded but partially mitigated, queue ~3.9k, p95 8s.
dmitri: thanks team. After action items: RCA on driver v525.42, test rollback in staging, autoscaler should validate quota before mass scale requests, improve early-detection alerts for driver Xid spikes.
pagerduty-bot: Incident status updated: Mitigated (partial) — monitoring.
chris: recording timeline and actions in postmortem draft. Will link here when ready.
emily: quick note: remember to add metric for effective GPU capacity (available - driver_down) to alert earlier.
alex: end of handoff. I'll escalate if cloud quota change comes through.
